audit.title: Chainlink Automation Service Limits
audit.summary: This is a short, single-table reference page listing per-chain log-processing limits for Chainlink Automation log-trigger upkeeps. Its biggest strength is the concrete, per-chain quantitative table — exactly the kind of specific fact generative engines lift. Its biggest opportunity is discoverability: the page carries no JSON-LD, canonical, or freshness metadata, its title promises broader "service limits" than it delivers, and no heading is phrased as the symptom question a developer would actually ask ("why is my upkeep missing logs?"). The honest verdict: strong data, thin packaging — it will be under-retrieved relative to the value of its numbers.

recommendations.title: Lead the section with the answer
recommendations.where: under `## Maximum logs processed for log trigger upkeeps`
recommendations.issue: "Chainlink Automation nodes look back over a limited range…" — process first, number last.
recommendations.change: Insert a first sentence: "Chainlink Automation processes 1–20 logs per block per upkeep depending on the chain (20 on Ethereum, 4 on most L2s, 1 on Gnosis); see the table below." Keep the existing prose after it.
recommendations.why: the first liftable sentence should carry the canonical fact so skim/RAG chunks stand alone.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/query-phrased heading
recommendations.issue: concept-titled "Maximum logs processed…" won't match how devs query.
recommendations.change: add an H3 or reword to include "Why is my log-trigger upkeep missing logs / not processing all events?" with the "configure a manual trigger as backup" answer directly beneath.
recommendations.why: engines retrieve symptom-phrased headings that concept prose loses, even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata
recommendations.issue: canonical MISSING; no dateModified; 0 JSON-LD blocks.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL, `dateModified`, and `inLanguage`; surface a visible "Last updated" line. Limits change over time — freshness is a trust signal here specifically.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T; canonical prevents `.md`/HTML duplicate ambiguity.

recommendations.title: Link out to canonical definitions
recommendations.where: first uses of "log trigger upkeep" and "minimum dequeue method"
recommendations.change: inline-link "log trigger upkeep" to its concept page and add a one-line definition of "minimum dequeue method (latest logs processed first)."
recommendations.why: attributable claims and crisp definitions raise citation rate and entity resolution.

recommendations.title: Make the table units explicit and dated
recommendations.issue: column header carries the unit; row values are bare integers, easy to lift out of context.
recommendations.change: keep the header but add a caption noting the unit and effective date, e.g. "Logs per block per upkeep, as of {date}."
recommendations.why: a lifted row/number retains meaning without its header.

recommendations.title: Reconcile scope of title vs content
recommendations.issue: title implies all service limits; body covers only log-trigger log counts.
recommendations.change: either broaden the page with other limits (gas, check/perform limits) or add an intro line and links pointing to where the other limits live.
recommendations.why: aligns retrieval expectations and enables full-lifecycle coverage.

antiPatterns: Mild answer-buried-in-prose: the section opens with mechanism rather than the limit.
Undated content: no visible last-updated on a page whose numbers are time-sensitive.
No unresolved cross-references, no keyword stuffing, no fluff — prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced — good; confirm this page is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Site-level JSON-LD/`TechArticle` templating and canonical emission are platform concerns best fixed once across `docs.chain.link` rather than per page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served HTML; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
